limits: the runner set is matched by call name: a locally defined function named run/sh/git is indistinguishable from the real runner, so the audit classifies by call-spelling, not by the callee's body

measured means the expression derives from a call spelled as a runner somewhere in its name chain, not that the call ran the command the state claims (a sh(["true"]).returncode passes while running nothing relevant); the claim is provenance, not command identity

branch reachability is approximated by requiring every pre-call assignment to be measured, so a correct driver that assigns a literal only in an unreachable branch is flagged (conservative); control flow is not analyzed
only bare-name add(...) calls are sites: a method call (c.add(...)) or a differently named recorder is zero-site and passes vacuously

the expectation (want_code) is data and is not classified, so a driver whose want_code is the recorded expression makes the comparison tautological and still audits green; the committed driver's expectations are literals
